Name: Izapa Archaeological Zone
Brief Description: Olmec-Maya bridge site (1500 BCE-1200 CE) with 89 stelae including famous Tree of Life stela, aligned with Tacana Volcano

Name: Finca Argovia
Brief Description: Historic German coffee plantation from 1880 with boutique hotel, organic coffee tours, 187 hectares of rainforest

Name: Finca Hamburgo
Brief Description: 1888 German coffee plantation at 1249m elevation, museum, views of Volcan Tacana, coffee tours and tastings

Name: Tapachula Parque Central
Brief Description: City center with Casa de Cultura (Art Deco 1929), Church of San Agustin, markets and colonial architecture

Name: Tacana Volcano
Brief Description: Mexico-Guatemala border volcano at 4060m, sixth-highest peak in Mexico, dominates Tapachula landscape

Name: Lake Coatepeque
Brief Description: Volcanic crater lake, one of largest in Central America, activities include kayaking, swimming, fishing

Name: Mirador Cerro El Baul
Brief Description: Viewpoint with panoramic views of Coatepeque region and monument to Tecun Uman

Name: Quetzaltenango Central Park
Brief Description: Heart of Xela with Teatro Municipal (1895), cathedral, colonial architecture, local markets

Name: Teatro Municipal Quetzaltenango
Brief Description: Neoclassical theater built 1895, known for jazz performances and Juegos Florales literary contest

Name: Volcan Santa Maria
Brief Description: Perfect cone volcano at 3770m towering over Quetzaltenango, popular for hiking

Name: Volcan Santiaguito
Brief Description: Active volcano at 2500m with frequent small eruptions visible from viewpoints, sunrise hikes available

Name: Laguna Chicabal
Brief Description: Sacred crater lake atop volcano, Mayan ceremonial site with cloud forest, spiritual significance

Name: Fuentes Georginas
Brief Description: Natural thermal hot springs from Zunil Volcano, surrounded by rainforest and ferns

Name: Salcaja La Conquistadora
Brief Description: First cathedral in Central America built 1524, famous for Rompope fermented fruit broth

Name: Lake Atitlan Overview
Brief Description: Volcanic caldera lake at 1562m, 340m deep, surrounded by three volcanoes and 11 Maya villages

Name: Volcan San Pedro
Brief Description: 3020m volcano, most popular for hiking from San Pedro La Laguna, 3-5 hour summit hike

Name: Volcan Toliman
Brief Description: 3158m volcano with two peaks and imploded crater, cloud forest trails, 3-5 hour hike

Name: Volcan Atitlan
Brief Description: 3535m active volcano (last erupted 1856), most challenging hike, overnight camping recommended

Name: Santiago Atitlan Town
Brief Description: Largest traditional Tz'utujil Maya town on Lake Atitlan at 1568m, rich cultural traditions

Name: Parroquia Santiago Apostol
Brief Description: Colonial church in Santiago Atitlan, 16th-century architecture, focal point of community

Name: Maximon Shrine Santiago
Brief Description: Shrine to Maya-Catholic folk saint Maximon (San Simon), moves annually, offerings include tobacco and candles

Name: Parque de Paz Santiago
Brief Description: Civil War memorial to 1990 massacre where 14 civilians killed, somber historical reminder

Name: Rey Tepepul Nature Reserve
Brief Description: Cloud forest reserve for quetzal bird viewing, early morning guided hikes, monkeys and rare birds

Name: San Juan La Laguna
Brief Description: Art galleries, textile cooperatives, colorful murals, women's weaving workshops with natural dyes

Name: San Pedro La Laguna
Brief Description: Backpacker hub with volcano hiking, restaurants, nightlife, Spanish schools

Name: San Marcos La Laguna
Brief Description: Wellness center of lake with yoga, meditation, reiki, holistic therapies, peaceful atmosphere

Name: Panajachel
Brief Description: Main tourist hub with Santander Street markets, boat departure point for lake villages

Name: Antigua Parque Central
Brief Description: Central plaza with reconstructed fountain, surrounded by cathedral, Palace of Captains, cafes

Name: Arco de Santa Catalina
Brief Description: Iconic yellow arch built 1693 connecting convent to school, frames Volcan de Agua perfectly

Name: La Merced Church
Brief Description: Spectacular Baroque yellow facade with intricate details, large fountain in courtyard, active church

Name: Cathedral San Jose Antigua
Brief Description: Main cathedral on plaza, mixture of active church and earthquake ruins, significant religious landmark

Name: Cerro de la Cruz Viewpoint
Brief Description: Hilltop viewpoint overlooking Antigua and Volcan de Agua, 15-20 minute walk, best at sunset

Name: Convento de Capuchinas
Brief Description: Well-preserved convent ruins with unique circular architecture, beautiful example of colonial religious architecture

Name: Museo Casa Santo Domingo
Brief Description: Former monastery now hotel and museum with colonial art, archaeology, Mayan artifacts, beautiful gardens

Name: ChocoMuseo Antigua
Brief Description: Interactive chocolate-making workshops, bean-to-bar process, family-friendly Guatemalan chocolate experience

Name: Volcan de Agua
Brief Description: 3760m perfect cone volcano dominating Antigua skyline, can be climbed with guide

Name: Volcan de Fuego
Brief Description: 3763m very active volcano with frequent eruptions visible from Antigua, not climbable due to danger

Name: Volcan Acatenango
Brief Description: 3976m volcano with popular overnight camping trips to watch Fuego erupt, challenging but spectacular

Name: Finca Filadelfia Antigua
Brief Description: Coffee plantation with tours showing bean-to-cup process, tastings with different brewing methods
